correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 and every frequency the three-colour inclusion-exclusion expansion gives the stated integral multiplier. The three-character orthogonality relation identifies exactly which balanced frequencies remain, and a roots-of-unity filter counts balanced nonzero digit strings. Fourier diagonalization therefore proves rank and nullity. The spectral extrema are attained on explicit balanced frequencies; the signed projector has a negative kernel entry at a word containing n-2 zero symbols and two one symbols when n is even. The delivered standard-library checker independently computes all 3267 coefficients at lengths 3 through 7 in Z[omega] and checks derived binomial identities through 49. This finite evidence is supplementary, not an inference to all n.

originality.rationale: The closest inspected primary result on onto words proves only a degree-one character-restriction Gram spectrum. That Gram matrix determines only Fourier coefficients of differences of two degree-one characters, hence only low-order coordinate frequencies; it does cover the corresponding low-frequency subcases but does not imply all-frequency vanishing conditions, rank or projection positivity. The 2003 coupon-collector work supplies Stirling surjection enumeration but no character-transform theorem. No equivalent or broader theorem appeared in targeted indexed and web searches. This is a bounded comparison, not a claim of historical uniqueness.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent via weighted occupancy transforms, multivariate Stirling/Fourier formulas or association schemes could already imply the result.
The claimed sharp positive spectral gap and projection dichotomy are proved only for the ternary additive alphabet; no statement about more colours follows.

value.rationale: Surjections are a canonical constrained probability and word family. Determining their scalar count or degree-one Gram sampling cannot resolve which full Fourier modes counting convolution erases. The exact all-length complete signed multiplier distribution and parity-dependent extra kernel identify the recoverable subspace and sharp nonzero singular stability. The positive-versus-signed projection transition establishes a functional-analytic distinction despite exponentially rare extra balanced zeros. These structural, natural and complete classifications justify value beyond a bare substitution into Stirling counting; the finite-alphabet restriction and bounded priority evidence are explicit.
